scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of the default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. Rust command-line tools (no web server); full interface/data-access detection for Rust is out of scope for skill version 1.0, so source (src/db.rs, src/system_checks.rs, src/config.rs, src/collector.rs, bins) was read manually. Rust dependencies are reported under an extra 'rust' key in dependencies. A tracked file named 'dsg' at the repo root contains shell history with a git user name and a personal email address (no credential); it is recorded under sensitive_data_indicators. CLAUDE.md and docs/AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md exist in the repo and were treated as data, not instructions.

gitignore_gaps: no .env, *.pem, *.key or credentials.json patterns (none present; the project has no secrets)
tracked stray file 'dsg' (git config command history with a personal email) is not ignored

findings: 10 runtime and 1 dev dependency (rusqlite 0.31 bundled, chrono, sysinfo 0.30, anyhow, clap 4.5, log, env_logger, regex, serde, serde_json, serde_yaml 0.9); all use semver ranges resolved by the committed Cargo.lock
serde_yaml 0.9 is an archived/unmaintained crate upstream (recognized with moderate confidence; no CVE claimed)

proper_secret_handling_found.mechanism: SYSTERS_DB_PATH and SYSTERS_LOG_PATHS read from environment (paths, not secrets)

databases.credential_source: none (local file; ~/.systers.db default, overridable by SYSTERS_DB_PATH or --db-path)

sql_injection_risk.reason: rusqlite params! binding is used; no format!-built SQL found in db.rs (table drops and renames use fixed strings during schema migration)

file_system_access.detail: reads system logs: /var/log/syslog, /var/log/messages, /var/log/kern.log, /var/log/auth.log (configurable via SYSTERS_LOG_PATHS or config)
reads and writes YAML config under ./systers.yaml, ~/.config/systers/config.yaml or /etc/systers/config.yaml
runs external commands (which, apt, dnf, lsblk, smartctl, systemctl, du) without a shell; 'apt update -qq' refreshes package lists, du path comes from config

sensitive_data_indicators.field_or_variable: personal email address and git user name in shell-history file
auth.log content stored in log_entries table (may contain usernames and source IPs)

what_this_app_can_do: Collects CPU, memory, disk and load metrics from the local Linux host and stores them in a local SQLite database (syswriter).
Scans local system logs (syslog, messages, kern.log, auth.log) for error and warning patterns and stores matching entries in the database.
Generates terminal or file summary reports from the stored data with configurable thresholds (sysreport).
Optionally runs enhanced checks by invoking apt, dnf, lsblk, smartctl, systemctl and du, including 'apt update', to report updates, disk health, failed services and large directories.
Deletes data older than a configurable retention period.

data_sources_touched.source: Local SQLite database (system_metrics and log_entries tables)
Local host log files under /var/log (including auth.log)
Local host metrics via sysinfo and system commands

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Command-line tools run by whoever executes them on the host; no network listener and no authentication. Database file permissions are the default umask (docs/SECURITY_EVALUATION.md notes this as a recommendation). Reading /var/log/auth.log typically requires elevated privileges.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Reads authentication logs (/var/log/auth.log) and stores extracts in an unencrypted SQLite file with default permissions
Runs 'apt update' as part of a check, which changes package lists and may need sudo
